title: introduce-fast-fail-downgrade-detector-and-transactional-backup-index
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: private deployments need fast, deterministic failure modes on attempted downgrades and an atomic mapping between backup artifacts and on-disk schema versions to make restores safe and auditable. This PR introduces two complementary features: 1) a fast-fail Downgrade Detector that runs as part of the installer and as a preflight Helm hook to abort upgrades/downgrades when incompatible binary/schema combinations are detected; 2) a Transactional Backup Index that records backup UUIDs, manifest checksums, schema_version, and operator generation into a single append-only index stored alongside backups. Together they reduce blind downgrades and make restores idempotent and verifiable. Changes include: Helm: adds pre-upgrade and pre-delete hooks (job) that invoke the downgrade-detector binary and surface clear exit codes for Helm to surface; CLI/Installer: introduces "redwoodctl migration verify-downgrade" and integration with the installer preflight runner; Backup subsystem: new indexer service and an index format (compact newline-delimited JSON entries) plus a restore verifier that consults the index to ensure atomicity; Terraform: updates module for S3/GCS backup bucket lifecycle and adds optional DynamoDB-based index storage for high-availability state locking; Tests/docs: adds end-to-end Canary that simulates multi-tenant restore and a short operator runbook for triage. See checklist: - [x] Downgrade detector binary + unit tests - [x] Helm hooks and chart changes - [x] Transactional backup indexer and index format docs - [x] Terraform module wiring and state locking option - [x] End-to-end canary test and runbook - [x] Backwards-compatible: index is optional and enabled via config. Impact: this is non-breaking by default but enables stronger safety when configured. Rollout plan: staged rollout to release/* clusters, enable indexer in Dedicated/private beta, monitor restore-success-rate metric and index-consistency alarms.
